# Set Up Workspace

```{r,  warning=F, message=F}
# Load packages
library(dplyr) #For easier data manipulation
library(readr) #For reading in data
library(psych) #For computing summary statistics and Cronbach's alpha
library(broom) #For organizing output of statistical models
library(pwr) #For power analysis
library(mediation) #For testing mediation models
library(ggeffects) #For generating predicted values from models for plotting
library(ggplot2) #For graphing
library(scales) #For adjusting plot axis scales
library(Cairo) #For better graphic rendering
library(extrafont) #For modifying fonts on graphs
library(printr) #For simple table outputs in Rmarkdown
library(kableExtra) #For outputting clean tables
library(papaja) #For reporting results in APA format
select <- dplyr::select #Ensuring that the default for "select" is from dplyr

# Set up plot theme
## (Thanks to John Sakaluk for this particular setup: 
## https://sakaluk.wordpress.com/2015/08/27/6-make-it-pretty-plotting-2-way-interactions-with-ggplot2/#APA)
apatheme <- theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line())

# Regression Display Function
## This function is useful for rounding estimates and displaying CIs alongside other output.
display.lm <- function(model) {
  df <- summary(model) %>% with(df)
  display.obj <- tidy(model) %>% bind_cols(confint_tidy(model)) %>% 
    as.data.frame() %>% mutate(p.value.char = ifelse(p.value < .001, "< .001", p.value),
                               p.value.3 = round(p.value, 3),
                               ` ` = ifelse(p.value < .001, "***", 
                                            ifelse(p.value < .01, "**", 
                                                   ifelse(p.value < .05, "*", 
                                                          ifelse(p.value < .10, ".", " "))))) %>%
    mutate(p.value = as.character(ifelse(p.value < .001, "< .001", p.value.3)),
           df = df[2]) %>%
    select(term, B = estimate, SE = std.error, t = statistic, df, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, ` `) %>%
    mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)
  return(display.obj)
}

## Additional steps for formatting kable
kable.lm <- function(display.obj) {
  kable(display.obj, align = c("l", rep('c', ncol(display.obj) - 1))) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed", "responsive"), 
                  full_width = F, position = "center")
}

# T-Test Display Function
## This function is useful for giving summary statistics and Cohen's d along with t-test output
display.t <- function(y, x, type = "ind", var.equal = T) {
  tmp <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

  if(type=="ind") {
    desc <- describeBy(tmp$y, group = tmp$x, mat = T)
    Ms <- desc$mean
    SDs <- desc$sd
    t.out <- t.test(tmp$y ~ tmp$x, var.equal = var.equal)
    d.out <- effsize::cohen.d(tmp$y, tmp$x)
  }
  if(type=="dep") {
    desc <- describe(tmp)
    Ms <- desc$mean
    SDs <- desc$sd
    t.out <- t.test(tmp$y, tmp$x, var.equal = var.equal, paired = T)
    d.out <- effsize::cohen.d(tmp$y, tmp$x, paired = T)
  }
  out <- tidy(t.out) %>%
    mutate(Mean1 = Ms[1], SD1 = SDs[1], Mean2 = Ms[2], SD2 = SDs[2],
           p.value.char = as.character(ifelse(p.value < .001, "< .001", round(p.value, 3)))) %>%
    mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 3) %>%
    select(Mean1, SD1, Mean2, SD2, t = statistic, df = parameter,
           p = p.value.char) %>%
    mutate(d = d.out$estimate) %>%
    mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)
  return(out)
}
```

```{r}
describe(S1.full$age) %>% select(mean, sd, median, min, max) %>% round(2)
```

<br>

#### Exclusion Criteria {#exclusion}

First, we exclude any cases for which the message would be pro-attitudinal (i.e., attitudes toward recycling below the midpoint.) The following table indexes the number of people who met the inclusion criteria ("TRUE") in each condition.

```{r}
# Computing average initial attitudes
S1.full <- S1.full %>% mutate(att1 = (att1_1 + att1_2 + att1_3) / 3) 

#Counting number of negative attitudes in each condition
table(S1.full$cond.F, S1.full$att1 >= 0) 

#Reducing data down to those with positive attitudes
S1 <- filter(S1.full, att1 >= 0) 
```

<br>

Next, we excluded any cases that were duplicates of a previous participant's IP Address. For confidentiality and privacy, actual IP Addresses are not included in shared data. Rather, the variable "duplicatedIP" was computed from the syntax: `duplicated(IPAddress)` and thus codes for whether an instance of an IP Address in the data was a duplicate of a previous one. "TRUE" in the table below is the number of cases that **are** duplicated IP Addresses (n = `r sum(S1$duplicatedIP)`; `r round(sum(S1$duplicatedIP)/nrow(S1), 4)*100`% of the remaining sample).

```{r}
# Counting number of duplicated IP Addresses
table(S1$duplicatedIP)
table(S1$duplicatedIP) %>% prop.table() %>% round(4)

# Reducing data by excluding duplicated IP Addresses
S1 <- filter(S1, duplicatedIP == F)
```

<br>

Final sample size: `nrow(S1)` = `r nrow(S1)`.

<br>

#### Power Analysis

```{r}
pwr.f2.test(u = 1, #df for numerator; conducting the analysis for the single interaction term
            v = (nrow(S1) - 3 - 1), #df for denominator; N - 3 [number of total regression terms] - 1
            sig.level = .05, 
            power = .80)
```

<br>

### Independent Variables

#### Pre-Message Attitudes

Cronbach's alpha (`std.alpha`) for the three pre-message attitude items:

```{r}
select(S1, att1_1, att1_2, att1_3) %>% psych::alpha() %>% with(total) %>% round(2)
```

*Note that the composite for pre-message attitudes (`att1`) was computed above in the [exclusion criteria](#exclusion) section.

<br>

#### Counter-Attitudinal Message

(See the other Rmarkdown report on the OSF page for this project for a full report of all pilot tests, including text analyses of the messages.)

<br>

### Dependent Measures

#### Thought Listing

**Computing thought coding variables for each coder:**
```{r}
## Coder 1
S1$posA <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VA")) == 1, na.rm = T)
S1$negA <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VA")) == 2, na.rm = T)
S1$neuA <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VA")) == 3, na.rm = T)
S1$irrA <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VA")) == 4, na.rm = T)

## Coder 2
S1$posB <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VB")) == 1, na.rm = T)
S1$negB <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VB")) == 2, na.rm = T)
S1$neuB <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VB")) == 3, na.rm = T)
S1$irrB <- rowSums(select(S1, matches("Th[1-6]VB")) == 4, na.rm = T)
```

<br>

**Assessing coder agreement:**

```{r}
corr.pos <- cor.test(S1$posA, S1$posB) %>% tidy() %>% mutate(valence = "Positive Thoughts")
corr.neg <- cor.test(S1$negA, S1$negB) %>% tidy() %>% mutate(valence = "Negative Thoughts")
corr.neu <- cor.test(S1$neuA, S1$neuB) %>% tidy() %>% mutate(valence = "Neutral Thoughts")
corr.irr <- cor.test(S1$irrA, S1$irrB) %>% tidy() %>% mutate(valence = "Irrelevant Thoughts")
list(corr.pos, corr.neg, corr.neu, corr.irr) %>% do.call(rbind.data.frame, .) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(p = ifelse(p.value < .001, "< .001", p.value)) %>%
  select(valence, r = estimate, df = parameter, p) %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2) %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed", "responsive"), 
                full_width = F, position = "center") %>%
  column_spec(1, width = "12em")
```

<br>

**Consolidating coders' ratings:**

```{r}
### Average Thought Codings
S1$pos <- S1 %>% select(starts_with("pos")) %>% rowMeans()
S1$neg <- S1 %>% select(starts_with("neg")) %>% rowMeans()
S1$neu <- S1 %>% select(starts_with("neu")) %>% rowMeans()
S1$irr <- S1 %>% select(starts_with("irr")) %>% rowMeans()
```

<br>

**Computing composite thought valence variable:**

```{r}
S1 <- mutate(S1, cogres = (pos - neg) / (pos + neg + neu))

#Irrelevant-only responses will have a zero denominator; the intention is that they're zero
S1$cogres[is.nan(S1$cogres)] <- 0 
```

## Results

*First, we compute additional variables centering key predictors at "low" and "high" levels in order to decompose interactions later in the analysis.*

```{r}
S1$base_mor_low <- scale(S1$base_mor, scale = F) + sd(S1$base_mor)
S1$base_mor_high <- scale(S1$base_mor, scale = F) - sd(S1$base_mor)
S1$base_mor_max <- S1$base_mor - 5
S1$cond_mor <- (S1$cond + 1) / 2
S1$cond_prac <- (abs(S1$cond - 1))/2
S1$ideology_low <- scale(S1$ideology, scale = F) + sd(S1$ideology, na.rm = T)
S1$ideology_high <- scale(S1$ideology, scale = F) - sd(S1$ideology, na.rm = T)
```

### Persuasion Effects

In order to interpret the direction of these effects more easily, we reverse-code attitudes. Therefore, higher values on the attitudes variable indicated for **negative** attitudes toward recycling, which are more **message-consistent** attitudes. Therefore, higher values signal greater persuasion and lower values signal greater resistance.

```{r}
S1 <- S1 %>% mutate(att.pre = 0 - att1,
                    att.post = 0 - att2)
```

<br>

**Main Effects:**

```{r}
pers.ME <- lm(att.post ~ att.pre + cond + base_mor, S1)
display.lm(pers.ME) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Interaction:**

```{r}
pers.int <- lm(att.post ~ att.pre + cond * base_mor, S1)
display.lm(pers.int) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

Effect size for the interaction:

As presented by @selyaPracticalGuideCalculating2012:

$$f^{2} = \frac{R^2_{AB} - R^2_{A}}{1-R^2_{AB}}$$

```{r, results='asis'}
R2.ME <- summary(pers.ME) %>% with(r.squared)
R2.Full <- summary(pers.int) %>% with(r.squared)
f2 <- round((R2.Full - R2.ME)/(1 - R2.Full), 2)
print(paste("$f^{2}$ = ", f2))
```

### Mediation by Valenced Thoughts

#### Interaction

```{r}
cogres.int <- lm(cogres ~ cond * base_mor, S1)
display.lm(cogres.int) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

Effect size for the interaction:

```{r, results = 'asis'}
R2.ME.cogres <- summary(lm(cogres ~ cond + base_mor, S1)) %>% with(r.squared)
R2.Full.cogres <- summary(cogres.int) %>% with(r.squared)
f2.cogres <- round((R2.Full.cogres - R2.ME.cogres)/(1 - R2.Full.cogres), 2)
print(paste("$f^{2}$ = ", f2.cogres))
```

<br>

Note that the interaction does not change appreciably when covarying initial attitudes:

```{r}
lm(cogres ~ att.pre + cond * base_mor, S1) %>% display.lm() %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>
<br>

#### Indirect Effect

```{r}
S1$int <- S1$cond * S1$base_mor
model.y <- lm(att.post ~ int + cogres + att.pre + cond + base_mor, S1)
model.m <- lm(cogres ~ int + att.pre + cond + base_mor, S1)
```

**Effect of Thoughts on Post-Message Attitudes**

```{r}
display.lm(model.y) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Indirect Effect**

The following useds the **mediation** package to test the indirect effect of the interaction (`int`) on post-message attitudes (`att.post`) via cognitive responses (`cogres`). In the output, **"ACME"** ("Average Casual Mediation Effect") is the indirect effect.

```{r}
med.model <- mediation::mediate(model.m, model.y, treat = "int", mediator = "cogres", 
                                boot = TRUE, sims = 10000, conf.level = .95)
summary(med.model)
```

# Study 2

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
S2.full <- read_csv("data/MoralPersuasionData_Study2.csv")
```

## Method 

### Participants

#### Sample Size and Demographics

**Gender:**

```{r}
table(S2.full$gender)
```

*"Other" responses:*

```{r}
filter(S2.full, !is.na(d_gen_4_TEXT)) %>% select(d_gen_4_TEXT)
```

<br>

**Age:**

```{r}
describe(S2.full$age) %>% select(mean, sd, median, min, max) %>% round(2)
```

<br>

#### Exclusion Criteria {#exclusion2}

First, we exclude any cases for which the message would be pro-attitudinal (i.e., attitudes toward recycling below the midpoint.) The following table indexes the number of people who met the inclusion criteria ("TRUE") in each condition.

```{r}
# Computing average initial attitudes
S2.full <- S2.full %>% mutate(att1 = (att1_1 + att1_2 + att1_3) / 3,
                              att.pre = 0 - att1) #Reverse scoring attitudes as in Study 1 

#Counting number of negative attitudes in each condition
table(S2.full$cond.F, S2.full$att1 >= 0) 

#Reducing data down to those with positive attitudes
S2 <- filter(S2.full, att1 >= 0) 
```

<br>

Next, we excluded any cases that were duplicates of a previous participant's IP Address. For confidentiality and privacy, actual IP Addresses are not included in shared data. Rather, the variable "duplicatedIP" was computed from the syntax: `duplicated(IPAddress)` and thus codes for whether an instance of an IP Address in the data was a duplicate of a previous one. "TRUE" in the table below is the number of cases that **are** duplicated IP Addresses (n = `r sum(S2$duplicatedIP)`; `r round(sum(S2$duplicatedIP)/nrow(S2), 4)*100`% of the remaining sample).

```{r}
# Counting number of duplicated IP Addresses
table(S2$duplicatedIP)
table(S2$duplicatedIP) %>% prop.table() %>% round(4)

# Reducing data by excluding duplicated IP Addresses
S2 <- filter(S2, duplicatedIP == F)
```

<br>

Finally, we excluded a small number of extreme outliers on the dependent variable. In light of issues with mean-based methods of labeling outliers, we used median absolute deviations (a modified Z-score) to flag extreme scores on the dependent measure. See @iglewiczHowDetectHandle1993 and @leysDetectingOutliersNot2013 for relevant background and tutorials.

Essentially, this modified Z-score uses median absolute deviations (MAD) from the median as a modified standard deviation and indexes how many MADs an observation is from the median. (As it happens, using regular Z-scores produces similar scores.)

```{r}
# Compute composite post-message attitude variable
S2 <- mutate(S2, att2 = (att2_1 + att2_2 + att2_3) / 3,
             att.post = 0 - att2) #Reverse scoring attitudes as in Study 1

# Compute modified Z (using median instead of mean)
S2 <- S2 %>% mutate(att.post.modZ = abs(att.post - median(att.post)) / mad(att.post))
```

<br>

In the following analyses, we adopt a conservative cutoff of **4**. Nevertheless, @iglewiczHowDetectHandle1993 recommend 3.5 as a cutoff, and it can be a tricky business deciding on a cutoff. We present additional analyses in the supplement.

```{r}
S2 <- filter(S2, att.post.modZ < 4)
```

<br>

Final sample size: `nrow(S2)` = `r nrow(S2)`.

<br>

#### Power Analysis

```{r}
pwr.f2.test(u = 1, #df for numerator; conducting the analysis for the single interaction term
            f2 = .02,
            sig.level = .05, 
            power = .80)
```

<br>

### Independent Variables

#### Pre-Message Attitudes

Cronbach's alpha (`std.alpha`) for the three pre-message attitude items:

```{r}
select(S2, att1_1, att1_2, att1_3) %>% psych::alpha() %>% with(total) %>% round(2)
```

*Note that the composite for pre-message attitudes (`att1`) was computed above in the [exclusion criteria](#exclusion2) section.

<br>

#### Counter-Attitudinal Message

(See the other Rmarkdown report on the OSF page for this project for a full report of all pilot tests, including text analyses of the messages.)

<br>

### Dependent Measures

#### Thought Listing

**Computing total numbers of each kind of thought:**

Note that "Positive" = Message-Favorable, which is technically "against legalization".


```{r}
S2$pos <- rowSums(select(S2, matches("rate[1-6]")) == 2, na.rm = T)
S2$neg <- rowSums(select(S2, matches("rate[1-6]")) == 1, na.rm = T)
S2$neu <- rowSums(select(S2, matches("rate[1-6]")) == 3, na.rm = T)
S2$irr <- rowSums(select(S2, matches("rate[1-6]")) == 4, na.rm = T)
```

<br>

**Computing composite thought valence variable:**

```{r}
S2 <- mutate(S2, cogres = (pos - neg) / (pos + neg + neu))

#Irrelevant-only responses will have a zero denominator; the intention is that they're zero
S2$cogres[is.nan(S2$cogres)] <- 0 
```

<br>

#### Post-Message Attitudes

Cronbach's alpha (`std.alpha`) for the three post-message attitude items:

```{r}
# Cronbach's alpha
select(S2, att2_1, att2_2, att2_3) %>% psych::alpha() %>% with(total) %>% round(2)

```

<br>

#### Political Orientation

Cronbach's alpha (`std.alpha`) for the two ideology questions:

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
select(S2, poli_soc, poli_econ) %>% psych::alpha() %>% with(total) %>% round(2)
```

<br>

Summary statistics for ideology composite:

```{r}
# Compute political orientation index
S2 <- S2 %>% mutate(ideology = (poli_soc + poli_econ) / 2) 

# Get summary statistics for political orientation
psych::describe(S2$ideology) %>% select(mean, sd, median, min, max) %>% round(2)
```

## Results

*First, we compute additional variables centering key predictors at "low" and "high" levels in order to decompose interactions later in the analysis.*

```{r}
S2$base_mor_low <- scale(S2$base_mor, scale = F) + sd(S2$base_mor)
S2$base_mor_high <- scale(S2$base_mor, scale = F) - sd(S2$base_mor)
S2$base_mor_max <- S2$base_mor - 5
S2$cond_mor <- (S2$cond + 1) / 2
S2$cond_prac <- (abs(S2$cond - 1))/2
S2$ideology_low <- scale(S2$ideology, scale = F) + sd(S2$ideology, na.rm = T)
S2$ideology_high <- scale(S2$ideology, scale = F) - sd(S2$ideology, na.rm = T)
```

### Persuasion Effects

In order to interpret the direction of these effects more easily, we reverse-code attitudes. Therefore, higher values on the attitudes variable indicated for **negative** attitudes toward recycling, which are more **message-consistent** attitudes. Therefore, higher values signal greater persuasion and lower values signal greater resistance.

```{r}
S2 <- S2 %>% mutate(att.pre = 0 - att1,
                    att.post = 0 - att2)
```

<br>

**Main Effects:**

```{r}
pers.ME <- lm(att.post ~ att.pre + cond + base_mor, S2)
display.lm(pers.ME) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Interaction:**

```{r}
pers.int <- lm(att.post ~ att.pre + cond * base_mor, S2)
display.lm(pers.int) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

Effect size for the interaction:

As presented by @selyaPracticalGuideCalculating2012:

$$f^{2} = \frac{R^2_{AB} - R^2_{A}}{1-R^2_{AB}}$$

```{r, results='asis'}
R2.ME <- summary(pers.ME) %>% with(r.squared)
R2.Full <- summary(pers.int) %>% with(r.squared)
f2 <- round((R2.Full - R2.ME)/(1 - R2.Full), 2)
print(paste("$f^{2}$ = ", f2))
```

### Mediation by Valenced Thoughts

#### Interaction


```{r}
cogres.int <- lm(cogres ~ cond * base_mor, S2)
display.lm(cogres.int) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

Effect size for the interaction:

```{r, results = 'asis'}
R2.ME.cogres <- summary(lm(cogres ~ cond + base_mor, S2)) %>% with(r.squared)
R2.Full.cogres <- summary(cogres.int) %>% with(r.squared)
f2.cogres <- round((R2.Full.cogres - R2.ME.cogres)/(1 - R2.Full.cogres), 2)
print(paste("$f^{2}$ = ", f2.cogres))
```

<br>

Note that the interaction does not change appreciably when covarying initial attitudes:

```{r}
lm(cogres ~ att.pre + cond * base_mor, S2) %>% display.lm() %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

#### Indirect Effect

```{r}
S2$int <- S2$cond * S2$base_mor
model.y <- lm(att.post ~ int + cogres + att.pre + cond + base_mor, S2)
model.m <- lm(cogres ~ int + att.pre + cond + base_mor, S2)
```

**Effect of Thoughts on Post-Message Attitudes**

```{r}
display.lm(model.y) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Indirect Effect**

The following useds the **mediation** package to test the indirect effect of the interaction (`int`) on post-message attitudes (`att.post`) via cognitive responses (`cogres`). In the output, **"ACME"** ("Average Casual Mediation Effect") is the indirect effect.

```{r}
med.model <- mediation::mediate(model.m, model.y, treat = "int", 
                                mediator = "cogres", boot = TRUE, sims = 10000, conf.level = .95)
summary(med.model)
```

# Alternative Analyses

Although we report effects on post-message attitudes, controlling for pre-message attitudes in the text, we also noted that similar effects occur when using attitude change scores as the dependent measure. Here we present the results from this approach that mirror those reported in the text.

## Study 1

```{r}
S1 <- mutate(S1, attchange = att1 - att2) #Message-consistent change index
```

### Moral Basis x Message Type

<br>

**Main Effects:**

```{r}
pers.ME.change <- lm(attchange ~ cond + base_mor, S1)
display.lm(pers.ME.change) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Interaction:**

```{r}
pers.int.change <- lm(attchange ~ cond * base_mor, S1)
display.lm(pers.int.change) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

Effect size for the interaction:

```{r, results = 'asis'}
R2.ME.change <- summary(pers.ME.change) %>% with(r.squared)
R2.Full.change <- summary(pers.int.change) %>% with(r.squared)
f2.change <- round((R2.Full.change - R2.ME.change)/(1 - R2.Full.change), 2)
print(paste("$f^{2}$ = ", f2.change))
```

<br>

**Message Effect at Highest (5) Moral Basis:**

```{r}
lm(attchange ~ cond * base_mor_max, S1) %>% display.lm() %>% 
  filter(term == "cond") %>% kable.lm()
```

```{r}
  filter(term == "base_mor") %>% kable.lm()
```

```{r}
  filter(term == "base_mor") %>% kable.lm()
```

**Message Effect at Low (-1 SD) Moral Basis:**

```{r}

  filter(term == "cond") %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

### Mediation by Cognitve Responses

```{r}
model.y.change <- lm(attchange ~ int + cogres + cond + base_mor, S1)
model.m.change <- lm(cogres ~ int + cond + base_mor, S1)
```

**Effect of Thoughts on Attitude Change**

```{r}
display.lm(model.y.change) %>% kable.lm()
```

<br>

**Indirect Effect**

The following useds the **mediation** package to test the indirect effect of the interaction (`int`) on attitude change (`attchange`) via cognitive responses (`cogres`). In the output, **"ACME"** ("Average Casual Mediation Effect") is the indirect effect.

```{r}
med.model.change <- mediation::mediate(model.m.change, model.y.change, 
                                       treat = "int", mediator = "cogres", 
                                       boot = TRUE, sims = 10000, conf.level = .95)
summary(med.model.change)
```

<br>
